A sold-out Rod Laver Arena in Melbourne Park sets the stage for the 2016 Australian Open men’s singles final, where Novak Djokovic and Andy Murray face off under the evening sky. sourceExcerpt:
Federer’s 2017 Australian Open Triumph

Roger Federer’s 2017 Australian Open victory stands out as one of the most extraordinary comebacks in tennis history. After knee surgery sidelined him for much of 2016 and saw his ranking fall to No. 17, Federer entered Melbourne Park determined to reclaim his form. Along the way, he dispatched four top-10 opponents—Tomas Berdych, Kei Nishikori, Alexander Zverev, and finally Rafael Nadal in a thrilling five-set final lasting three hours and 38 minutes.

The championship match saw Federer take the first and third sets, with Nadal responding in the second and fourth. In the decisive fifth set, Federer rallied from an early break to win five consecutive games and seal the title 6-4, 3-6, 6-1, 3-6, 6-3. This triumph not only earned him his 18th Grand Slam but also made him the first player since Mats Wilander in 1982 to defeat four top-10 opponents en route to a major title.
